why_next: WHY THIS DIRECTION AND NOT ANOTHER. Three facts drive it, and all three were verified at source by this Director rather than taken from the producer's framing. First, the label question cannot be decided with the instrument as frozen, and re-running it would be a repair, not research: the frozen COLD_REEXPLORATION baseline is a breadth-first crawl whose route is itself a shortest path and whose token sum is a superset of the re-acquisition path's responses, so re_derivation >= re_acquisition is forced and the FALSIFIES branch was unreachable for any execution (20 of 20 measurable items, derived/costs.json). Second, and more decisive for where to go, the cost question this packet was supposed to answer was never actually measured at depth. Every admitted item sits at crawl hop 0 or 1, where one or two unconditional GETs already reach it, so the entire re-acquisition-versus-re-derivation contrast was exercised in the extreme-favourable case for persistence; the packet therefore produced a negative-sounding artifact (byte-stable items cost exactly what re-deriving them costs) at the one depth where persistence is most likely to pay, and it says nothing about the depths where the amortization question actually bites. The unmeasured quantity, cost as a function of graph distance, is also the single input that C-FRESHNESS break-even arithmetic and the C-WEB-DYNAMICS timescales axis both lack, so measuring it is decision-changing in both directions rather than merely incremental. Third, the packet's own most transferable finding is a level-of-description fact rather than a Web fact: an item's stationarity class is not a property of the item but of the item AND the declared observation channel, because switching from a page-hash channel to a value-only channel leaves 12 of 29 classified items with NO class at all rather than moving them into a different class. Any successor that keeps a taxonomy must therefore declare the channel per item, and any successor that does not need a taxonomy should drop it entirely, which is what the proposed question does. ALTERNATIVES CONSIDERED AND WHY NOT. Re-freezing the same stationarity experiment with corrected rule order and a satisfiable comparator is a REPAIR with known fixes; it is a precondition of any future use of this instrument, not this lane's next research question, and doing it as the next experiment would be a fourth consecutive packet in the same basin, which is the local attractor the mandate itself flagged. Re-measuring the static re-derivable fraction was already ruled a repair by the inherited handoff and remains so. Re-entering the TERMINATED C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY deterministic-compilation-bypass thread is prohibited by the accepted record. Returning to C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE is blocked for three consecutive experiments by the unsatisfiable V9_CODE_HASHED_INTO_FREEZE control-plane defect that no lane can repair. Pursuing C-CROSSSITE's registered next_gate requires an executable induced mechanism in the committed kernel, which does not exist, so no frontier packet can discharge it. A program-wide instrument-certificate deliverable, for example a shared pre-execution attainability and control-receipt gate, is scientifically the highest-leverage action for the whole program but it is C-MEAS-VALID work owned by runtime and physics, not frontier work, so it is transmitted by artifact reference in verdict.claim_updates rather than proposed as frontier's own next experiment. established: THE FROZEN INSTRUMENT COULD NOT HAVE RETURNED EITHER OF ITS OWN ANSWERS, and this is the packet's load-bearing transferable result. The frozen falsifier's cost condition compares median shortest-path re-acquisition against median unconditional re-derivation produced by a breadth-first cold crawl; a BFS route is itself a shortest path and its token sum is a superset of the re-acquisition path's responses, so re_derivation >= re_acquisition on both units holds by construction. Verified at source by this Director from derived/costs.json: 20 classified items have a measurable re-derivation and 20 of 20 satisfy the inequality; all 7 reachable session_invariant items have re-acquisition EXACTLY equal to re-derivation, hence infinite item-level break-even; the class-level value of 1 to 34,299 that appears elsewhere in the packet is jitter on economically identical single GETs (bitbucket 445881 vs 445894 tokens gives 34299). Consequence for any successor: a falsifier that compares a shortest-path arm against a search-derived baseline can never trigger, and the missing FALSIFIES here is an artifact of instrument definition, not a bounded negative about handle persistence. Evidence: result.metrics.falsifier_triggered.attainability_audit with frozen_falsifier_trigger_region_is_empty=true and empirical_share=1.0; audit validity_findings AUDIT-VF-02; audit baseline_findings AUDIT-BF-01; OBS-17.

ON THIS HAND-PICKED CREDENTIAL-FREE GET-ONLY POOL, BOTH SERVER-MINTED CSRF HANDLES ROTATE INSIDE A SINGLE EPISODE. FOR THE BYTE-STABLE OBJECT CLASS AT CRAWL HOP 0 OR 1 THERE IS NO AMORTIZATION SURFACE TO BUY, stated precisely. AN ITEM'S STATIONARITY CLASS IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE ITEM; IT IS A PROPERTY OF THE ITEM AND THE DECLARED OBSERVATION CHANNEL. The 12 do not move to another class, they leave the taxonomy entirely, because the frozen five-class table has no class for 'value stable across sessions while the containing page churns' (unclassifiable_reason 'unmatched_by_frozen_table'). The apparent 12/5 split reported in result.metrics.value_only_sensitivity is therefore a denominator shrink from 29 to 17, and n_items_that_change_class_vs_primary=6 and VN-06's 'moves 12 of 29 items' are not accurate as written. Architectural consequence that does survive: any agent-visible freshness guard must be channel-conditional, because the same item is 'stable' or 'stale' depending on what is hashed.

THE STATIONARITY TAXONOMY ITSELF IS NOT IDENTIFIED BY ANY OBSERVED COUNT IN THIS PACKET. Three of the five classes have zero members and those zeros are zero BY CONSTRUCTION: derived/classification.json records time_scoped_and_rotating_reachable_under_frozen_order=false because the frozen evaluation order tests session_scoped before time_scoped and rotating, so any item with within-session variance can never reach the later classes.
